programming_tips.topic: Graphite Milling Fundamentals — Climb Milling ONLY
programming_tips.description: Graphite MUST be machined using climb milling (down-cut) exclusively. Conventional milling (up-cut) causes severe chipping on electrode edges and corners. Graphite does not form chips like metal — it fractures as dust particles. Climb milling pushes the fracture force into the bulk material, producing clean edges. Set CAM to climb-only for all 2D and 3D operations. This rule applies to ALL graphite grades from soft (EDM-3) to hard (POCO HK-6).
gotchas: NEVER use conventional milling on graphite — even briefly during tool entry causes edge chipping visible on EDM burn
Conventional entry moves in CAM must be replaced with ramp or helical entry
Tool path direction must be verified in simulation — a single conventional move can scrap an electrode
This applies to both roughing and finishing — no exceptions

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Shallow DOC + High Feed Strategy for Graphite
programming_tips.code_example:
(Graphite roughing — shallow DOC, high feed)
S25000 M03
M50 (dust collection ON)
G01 Z-0.3 F3000 (0.3mm DOC, 3000mm/min feed)
(Graphite finishing — very shallow, high speed)
S30000
G01 Z-0.05 F5000 (0.05mm DOC, 5000mm/min)
programming_tips.description: Graphite machining strategy is opposite to metal cutting: use very shallow depth of cut (0.1-0.5mm rough, 0.02-0.1mm finish) with very high feed rates (2000-8000 mm/min) and maximum RPM (25K-30K). Graphite is not plastically deformed — it fractures. Shallow cuts produce smaller fracture particles (finer dust) yielding better surface finish. Deep cuts cause large fractures that produce chipped surfaces unusable for precision EDM.
gotchas: Max DOC rough: 0.5mm in soft graphite, 0.3mm in fine-grain graphite (HK-15+)
Finish DOC: 0.02-0.05mm for Ra 0.4-0.8um surface finish
Feed rate can exceed 5000mm/min because graphite cutting forces are very low
Chip load per tooth: 0.02-0.05mm/tooth typical — tool geometry matters more than chip load

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: No Coolant — Dry or Air Blast ONLY
programming_tips.code_example:
M50 (dust collection ON — MANDATORY)
M52 (air blast ON — chip clearing)
S30000 M03
G01 ... (machining)
M53 (air blast OFF)
M51 (dust collection OFF — only after all cutting done)
programming_tips.description: Graphite must be machined DRY or with air blast only. NEVER use liquid coolant on graphite. Coolant turns graphite dust into an abrasive slurry that destroys way covers, linear scales, and bearings. Air blast (M52) is used for chip (dust) evacuation from deep pockets. The primary chip removal method is the dust collection system (M50), which MUST be active whenever the spindle is running. Some shops use ionized air (M100) to prevent static buildup that attracts graphite dust to machine surfaces.
gotchas: NEVER, under any circumstances, use flood coolant or mist coolant on graphite
Dust collection (M50) must be ON before first spindle start and OFF only after last spindle stop
Air blast pressure should be 3-4 bar — too high scatters dust past extraction system
Static charge on graphite dust attracts it to every surface — use ionizer (M100) if available
Graphite dust + moisture = conductive paste that can short electrical components

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.description: Use diamond-coated (CVD) or nano-grain carbide tools for graphite. Uncoated carbide wears 10-50x faster. Typical tools: 2-flute ball nose for 3D finishing, 2-flute flat end mill for 2D roughing. HSK-E32 holders with ER16 or ER11 collets. Maximum tool shank is 6mm for most electrode work — the RKY-1000N's small HSK-E32 taper is designed for small precision tools. Tool balance grade G2.5 at 30,000 RPM minimum. Use shrink-fit or precision collet holders — never side-lock.
gotchas: Uncoated carbide in graphite: tool life ~30 min. Diamond-coated: tool life 10-50 hours
Ball nose tools must have center-cutting geometry for graphite — non-center-cutting leaves witness mark at tool center
Maximum recommended tool diameter: 12mm. Larger tools exceed spindle power for any meaningful material removal
Tool runout must be <5um at 30K RPM — graphite surface finish is directly proportional to runout
Replace tools at first sign of edge rounding — dull tools cause edge chipping on electrodes

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Surface Finish Targets for EDM Electrode Quality
programming_tips.description: EDM electrode surface finish directly affects the EDM burn quality. Target surface finish on the electrode depends on the EDM application: Roughing electrode: Ra 1.6-3.2um (acceptable tool marks). Semi-finish electrode: Ra 0.8-1.6um. Finishing electrode: Ra 0.2-0.8um (mirror-like for text, logos, textures). Orbitless EDM electrode: Ra 0.1-0.4um. Use SSS control (G05 P2) for finishing electrodes to achieve Ra <0.4um on the RKY-1000N.
gotchas: Electrode surface roughness transfers to EDM cavity at approximately 1:1 ratio for fine EDM
Overburn per side must be accounted for in electrode size — typically 0.05-0.3mm depending on EDM settings
EDM rib electrodes require better finish than EDM pocket electrodes (ribs burn at higher VDI)
A Ra 0.4um electrode finish requires 0.02mm stepover with a 1mm ball nose at 30K RPM

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Dust Explosion Prevention — CRITICAL Safety Protocol
programming_tips.description: Graphite dust is a combustion hazard. Fine graphite particles (<50um) in airborne concentration >55 g/m3 are explosive when exposed to ignition source. The RKY-1000N dust extraction system is designed to maintain concentration well below this limit during normal operation. Key rules: (1) NEVER use compressed air to blow graphite dust, (2) ALWAYS run dust extraction during any cutting, (3) Clean machine with vacuum ONLY, (4) No open flames or sparking tools near the machine, (5) Ground all dust collection ducts to prevent static discharge.
gotchas: Graphite dust explosion is a REAL industrial hazard — not theoretical
Dust collector must be ATEX-rated or equivalent for combustible dust
Static electricity from graphite dust buildup can be an ignition source — use ionizer
Electrical cabinet filters must be anti-static rated to prevent dust accumulation causing shorts

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: G05 P2 SSS Control for Electrode Finishing
programming_tips.code_example:
G05 P2 (enable SSS — Super Smooth Surface)
S30000 M03
G01 ... F5000 (finishing passes — SSS smooths path)
G05 P0 (cancel SSS before tool change)
programming_tips.description: Mitsubishi SSS (Super Smooth Surface) control provides superior path interpolation smoothing for 3D contouring. Enables the controller to predictively smooth the tool path while maintaining surface tolerance. On the RKY-1000N, SSS combined with 30K RPM and 0.02mm stepovers produces mirror-finish electrodes (Ra 0.2-0.4um). SSS engages the 150-block lookahead buffer and dynamically adjusts feed rate at curvature transitions.
gotchas: SSS mode reduces feed rate at sharp transitions — actual feed may be 50% of programmed at tight corners
Cancel SSS (G05 P0) before tool change — leaving it active can cause erratic motion
SSS is most effective with small point-to-point distances (<0.1mm) from CAM
For Fanuc 31i controller option, use G05.1 Q1 instead of G05 P2

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Electrode Pallet System and G54.1 Multi-Electrode Setup
programming_tips.code_example:
G54.1 P1 (electrode 1 position on pallet)
(machine electrode 1)
G54.1 P2 (electrode 2 position)
(machine electrode 2)
(repeat for up to 48 electrodes per pallet)
programming_tips.description: The RKY-1000N is commonly used with electrode pallet systems (Erowa, System 3R, Hirschmann) that hold multiple electrode blanks. Each electrode position is a separate work offset in G54.1. Typical workflow: load pallet with electrode blanks, probe each blank to set G54.1 offsets, run batch program that machines all electrodes sequentially. This enables unattended electrode production of 10-50 electrodes per pallet.
gotchas: Always probe each electrode blank before machining — pallet repeatability is typically 2-5um, but blank positioning varies more
Use G10 L2 with probe results to automatically set G54.1 offsets from macro
Ensure dust extraction capacity is sufficient for extended unattended runs — check bin fullness before starting batch
Each electrode should have its own program or subprogram to allow individual recuts if quality check fails

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.topic: Tool Path Strategies for EDM Electrode Corners and Ribs
programming_tips.description: EDM electrode corners and thin ribs are the most failure-prone features in graphite machining. Sharp corners chip if the tool decelerates too aggressively. Thin ribs (<0.5mm) can snap if tool pressure is on the wrong side. Strategies: (1) Use constant-engagement toolpaths that maintain steady chip load around corners, (2) Approach all corners from the outside-in with climb milling, (3) For ribs <1mm thick, use ballnose tool radius equal to or smaller than half the rib thickness, (4) Reduce feed rate 30-50% when machining features thinner than 2x tool diameter.
gotchas: Corner chipping on electrodes produces visible defects in every EDM cavity — electrode corners are the highest-precision features
CAM corner rounding settings must be tighter than normal — use 0.005mm or less corner rounding tolerance
Thin rib electrodes: always machine both sides in the same operation to avoid thermal shift between setups
For ribs <0.3mm, consider wire EDM for the electrode rather than milling

source.handbook_title: Roku-Roku RKY-1000N High-Speed Machining Center Operator's Manual

programming_tips.code_example:
O0001 (ELECTRODE-001 FINISHING)
G00 G17 G40 G49 G54 G80 G90
M50 (dust collection ON — BEFORE any spindle start)
G28 G91 Z0 (home Z)
G28 G91 X0 Y0 (home XY)
T01 M06 (tool change)
G43 H01 Z50.0 (TLO at safe Z)
M52 (air blast ON)
S30000 M03 (spindle start at 30K)
(begin machining)
programming_tips.description: Graphite machine safe start MUST include dust collection activation (M50) before any spindle start. The sequence is: safety line, dust extraction ON, home axes, tool change, TLO, air blast, then spindle start. This ensures dust extraction is active before any dust-generating operation. At program end: spindle stop, air blast off, then dust extraction off AFTER a 10-second delay to clear residual airborne dust.
gotchas: CRITICAL: M50 must come BEFORE M03 in every program — running the spindle without dust extraction violates safety protocol
M51 (dust off) should include a G04 P10000 dwell (10 sec) to allow airborne dust to be captured
Include G49 in safe start — TLO errors are just as dangerous on graphite machines as metal machines
Program end: M05 (spindle stop), G04 P10000 (dwell), M53 (air off), G04 P5000 (dwell), M51 (dust off)
